events.factual_description: Keystone Korner Baltimore and its authorized InstantSeats listing present The Carl Filipiak Quartet featuring Lafayette Gilchrist on Sunday, November 29, 2026, with sets at 5:00 PM and 7:30 PM. The announced quartet is Carl Filipiak on guitar, Paul Hannah on saxophone, Tyler Bartram on bass and Mark St. Pierre on drums, with Lafayette Gilchrist on piano as special guest. InstantSeats states that this 2026 quartet is a fresh direction from Filipiak's earlier bands, is playing music by Bird, Trane and Miles alongside original jazz-inspired compositions, has a monthly residency and recording sessions underway, and is preparing an album for release later in 2026. The page identifies November 29 as the quartet's first appearance at Keystone Korner Baltimore. In-person face-value tickets are listed at $35-$40 plus fees for both sets; a separate $15 streaming pass is also offered.

en.why_it_matters: This is more than a familiar Baltimore pairing dropped onto a club calendar. Filipiak is bringing a newly configured quartet into Keystone Korner for the first time while the band is still being defined on record, and Gilchrist's piano adds another Baltimore voice with its own hard rhythmic pull. The combination of guitar, saxophone and Gilchrist's attack should let standards-derived language and fusion groove push against each other in a small room.
en.trip_verdict: From the DMV, I would make the Baltimore hop for this if the guitar-and-groove thread is calling: the room is intimate, the lineup is locally specific, and either set can anchor the evening without requiring a larger trip. I would choose one set rather than treat the date as a scarcity chase.

Filipiak lleva por primera vez a Keystone Korner esta nueva configuración de cuarteto justo cuando la banda todavía está tomando forma en disco, y el piano de Gilchrist agrega otra voz de Baltimore con un jalón rítmico muy propio. Guitarra, sax y el ataque de Gilchrist pueden poner a chocar el lenguaje que viene de los standards con el groove de fusión en una sala pequeña.

Escogería un set; no trataría la fecha como una persecución por escasez.
